Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them."

question: In Hebrews 7:26-27, what spotless character qualifies our High Priest, and how did His sacrifice differ from Levitical high priests?
opt1: Sinful, fallible, worldly, subject to daily errors; who needed annual sacrifices of bulls and goats to purify his own conscience
opt2: Holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; who needeth not daily... to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself
opt3: An angelic spirit who never walked the earth; who offered symbolic prayers rather than physical blood upon the altar
opt4: A mortal ruler who passed his office to his sons; who offered daily incense in the holy place of the tabernacle
correct: Holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; who needeth not daily... to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself
explanation: Our High Priest is morally flawless, elevated above the heavens, needing no repeated sacrifices for Himself, having completed our redemption once for all by offering Himself. Hebrews 7:26-27 (KJV) - "For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people's: for this he did once, when he offered up himself."

question: According to Hebrews 8:1, what is the 'sum' (chief point) of all the theological arguments presented concerning our High Priest?
opt1: We have an earthly priest residing in Jerusalem, who offers animal sacrifices daily
opt2: We have an angelic mediator standing before the veil, who reads written petitions
opt3: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens
opt4: We have a council of seventy elders, who govern civil disputes among believers
correct: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens
explanation: The central climax is that our High Priest is not serving in an earthly tent, but is seated in sovereign triumph at the right hand of God's throne in heaven. Hebrews 8:1 (KJV) - "Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;"

question: In Hebrews 8:2, of what sanctuary and tabernacle is Christ the ministering High Priest?
opt1: A minister of the stone temple built by Herod in Jerusalem
opt2: A minister of the portable wilderness tent stitched by the craftsmen of Israel
opt3: A minister of the symbolic academies founded by philosophers in Athens
opt4: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man
correct: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man
explanation: Christ ministers in the genuine, celestial archetype: the heavenly sanctuary erected directly by God rather than human hands. Hebrews 8:2 (KJV) - "A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man."

question: According to Hebrews 8:3, what essential duty is required of every high priest, and therefore of Christ as well?
opt1: Ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer
opt2: Ordained to collect municipal taxes for the Roman provincial treasury
opt3: Ordained to train young soldiers for physical warfare against pagan nations
opt4: Ordained to compose civic laws for the governance of Greek city-states
correct: Ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer
explanation: Because the priestly office inherently demands offering sacrifice, it was necessary that Christ offer His own body as the supreme sacrifice. Hebrews 8:3 (KJV) - "For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer."

question: In Hebrews 8:5, what warning did God give to Moses when constructing the tabernacle, proving it was merely a shadow of heavenly reality?
opt1: See that thou construct a magnificent palace exceeding the architectural temples of Egypt
opt2: See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount
opt3: See that thou collect gold and silver from all Gentile merchants passing through the desert
opt4: See that thou adapt the holy furniture according to the changing traditions of the tribes
correct: See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount
explanation: The earthly wilderness tabernacle was an exact physical reproduction (shadow) of the heavenly pattern revealed to Moses on Mount Sinai. Hebrews 8:5 (KJV) - "Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount."

question: According to Hebrews 8:6, how is Christ's ministry and covenant described in comparison to the Old Covenant?
opt1: A temporary ministry, by how much he is a reformer of the Mosaic code under Aaron
opt2: An earthly ministry, by how much he is an advisor to kings and governors
opt3: A more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises
opt4: A symbolic ministry, by how much he repeats the Levitical rituals in spiritual words
correct: A more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises
explanation: Christ's high-priestly ministry far surpasses the Levitical system, mediating a superior covenant founded upon eternal, gracious promises. Hebrews 8:6 (KJV) - "But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises."

question: In Hebrews 8:7-8, why was a second covenant sought, and with whom did the Lord announce He would make a New Covenant?
opt1: Because Moses lost the original stone tablets; therefore God made a covenant with the rulers of Rome
opt2: Because the first covenant was too lenient on sinners; therefore God made a covenant with the angels
opt3: Because the priests forgot the Levitical hymns; therefore God made a covenant with Greek scholars
opt4: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second; finding fault with them, he saith, I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah
correct: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second; finding fault with them, he saith, I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah
explanation: The inadequacy of the Old Covenant lay in human moral inability to keep it; hence God promised a New Covenant with Israel and Judah through Jeremiah. Hebrews 8:7-8 (KJV) - "For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:"

question: According to Hebrews 8:9, why did the Lord discard the covenant made with their fathers when He led them out of Egypt?
opt1: Because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord
opt2: Because they failed to conquer the fortified cities of Canaan within forty days
opt3: Because they refused to build stone temples in the wilderness of Sinai
opt4: Because they neglected to pay annual tribute to the priests of Aaron
correct: Because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord
explanation: The Sinai covenant failed because the people repeatedly broke their solemn vows, leading God to withdraw His covenant regard. Hebrews 8:9 (KJV) - "Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord."

question: In Hebrews 8:10, where does God promise to place and write His laws under the New Covenant?
opt1: I will engrave my laws upon marble tablets in the public market squares of Jerusalem
opt2: I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people
opt3: I will record my laws in secret books kept by the high priest inside the golden ark
opt4: I will carve my laws upon the gates of Roman cities to enforce civic compliance
correct: I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people
explanation: The New Covenant internalizes divine righteousness through regeneration, inscribing God's laws directly onto the minds and hearts of believers. Hebrews 8:10 (KJV) - "For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:"

question: What glorious promise of absolute divine forgiveness crowns the New Covenant in Hebrews 8:12?
opt1: For I will require annual animal sacrifices to remind them perpetually of their past guilt
opt2: For I will impose physical penances upon their children for seven generations
opt3: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more
opt4: For I will overlook sins only if they donate silver to the earthly temple treasury
correct: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more
explanation: Under the New Covenant, God grants complete, unreserved pardon, blotting out our sins from His judicial memory forever through Christ's atonement. Hebrews 8:12 (KJV) - "For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more."

question: In Hebrews 8:13, what does the pronouncement of a 'new' covenant signify regarding the old Mosaic system?
opt1: He hath confirmed the first covenant as permanently binding upon all Gentile believers
opt2: He hath merged both covenants into a single ceremonial code of physical washings
opt3: He hath declared that the Levitical priesthood will govern all nations during the millennium
opt4: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away
correct: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away
explanation: The very designation of 'New' declared the Old Covenant obsolete, aged, and destined to disappear with the destruction of the temple system. Hebrews 8:13 (KJV) - "In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away."

question: According to Hebrews 9:3-4, what sacred articles were contained in the Holiest of all behind the second veil?
opt1: The golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant
opt2: The seven-branched golden candlestick, the table of shewbread, and the altar of bronze
opt3: The stone monument of Moses, the sword of Joshua, and the royal crown of King David
opt4: The silver trumpets of assembly, the breastplate of Urim, and the vestments of Phinehas
correct: The golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant
explanation: The innermost sanctuary held the golden censer and the Ark of the Covenant, enshrining the golden pot of manna, Aaron's budded rod, and the two stone tablets of the Ten Commandments. Hebrews 9:3-4 (KJV) - "And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all; Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;"

question: In Hebrews 9:7, under what strict limitations did the high priest enter into the second tabernacle (Holiest of all)?
opt1: The high priest entered daily with all the elders, offering incense without any animal blood
opt2: Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people
opt3: The high priest entered every sabbath alongside the Levitical choir, singing prophetic hymns
opt4: The high priest entered at will whenever the congregation desired to consult the oracle
correct: Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people
explanation: Entry into the Holy of Holies was severely restricted: only the high priest, only once a year on the Day of Atonement, and never without sacrificial blood. Hebrews 9:7 (KJV) - "But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:"

question: What spiritual lesson was the Holy Ghost signifying through the structure of the earthly tabernacle, according to Hebrews 9:8?
opt1: That all Gentiles must be circumcised before entering the outer court
opt2: That angels alone were permitted to approach God's presence in prayer
opt3: The way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing
opt4: That animal sacrifices would continue unchanged throughout all eternity
correct: The way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing
explanation: The standing veil and restricted access showed that full, direct access to God's presence was not yet opened under the Old Covenant economy. Hebrews 9:8 (KJV) - "The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:"

question: According to Hebrews 9:9-10, what inherent limitation afflicted Levitical gifts and sacrifices?
opt1: They were too costly for ordinary citizens to purchase at the temple gates
opt2: They were rejected by God because they were not performed in the city of Rome
opt3: They purified the inward spirit but had no effect on external physical cleanliness
opt4: Could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed until the time of reformation
correct: Could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed until the time of reformation
explanation: Old Testament rituals dealt only with ceremonial, external purity; they lacked the power to cleanse the worshiper's guilty conscience, remaining temporary until Christ's reformation. Hebrews 9:9-10 (KJV) - "Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation."

question: In Hebrews 9:11-12, how did Christ enter the true heavenly sanctuary, and what eternal redemption did He secure?
opt1: By a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands; neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us
opt2: By the stone sanctuary of Herod; by the blood of bulls and lambs he entered annually, obtaining temporary pardon for one year
opt3: By the mystical spheres of the planets; by angelic incantations he entered repeatedly, obtaining political freedom for Israel
opt4: By the tabernacle of Moses; by water washings he entered every month, obtaining legal righteousness under the law
correct: By a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands; neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us
explanation: Christ bypassed earthly structures and animal blood, presenting His own sinless blood once for all in the heavenly sanctuary, securing eternal redemption. Hebrews 9:11-12 (KJV) - "But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us."

question: According to Hebrews 9:14, how much more efficacious is the blood of Christ, and to what end does it purge our conscience?
opt1: How much more shall the blood of Christ purchase earthly real estate to build churches across the Roman Empire?
opt2: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
opt3: How much more shall the blood of Christ exempt believers from paying taxes to civil governors?
opt4: How much more shall the blood of Christ grant physical immunity from mortal disease and sorrow?
correct: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
explanation: Offered through the eternal Spirit without moral blemish, Christ's blood purifies our inward conscience from dead ritualism to vibrant service to the living God. Hebrews 9:14 (KJV) - "How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?"

question: In Hebrews 9:16, what legal necessity must occur before a testament (covenant will) takes full legal effect?
opt1: The testament must be ratified by a majority vote of the municipal assembly
opt2: The testament must be sealed with the official signet ring of the Roman emperor
opt3: For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator
opt4: The testament must be read aloud in the temple courts for seven consecutive sabbaths
correct: For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator
explanation: Just as a human will cannot be executed while the testator lives, so the New Testament covenant was inaugurated through the sacrificial death of Christ. Hebrews 9:16 (KJV) - "For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator."

question: What foundational, absolute biblical principle regarding the remission of sins is declared in Hebrews 9:22?
opt1: And all things are purged by water baptism; and without ceremonial washings is no remission
opt2: And all things are purged by fasting; and without physical penance is no remission
opt3: And all things are purged by good deeds; and without monetary tithes is no remission
opt4: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission
correct: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission
explanation: God's holy justice establishes that forgiveness of sin requires an atoning blood sacrifice; without shedding of blood there is no remission. Hebrews 9:22 (KJV) - "And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission."

question: In Hebrews 9:24, where did Christ enter, and for what purpose does He appear now on our behalf?
opt1: For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us
opt2: Into the earthly sanctuary of Jerusalem, now to oversee the Levitical sacrifices of the priests
opt3: Into the subterranean caves of Mount Sinai, now to retrieve the original stone tablets of Moses
opt4: Into the municipal assembly halls of Rome, now to plead for the civil rights of Christians
correct: For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us
explanation: Christ entered heaven itself, the ultimate reality of which earthly tabernacles were mere copies, to represent us continually before the Father's face. Hebrews 9:24 (KJV) - "For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:"

question: According to Hebrews 9:27-28, what appointment is given unto all men, and how does Christ's second coming relate to believers?
opt1: It is appointed unto men to undergo repeated reincarnations until perfected: so Christ offers sacrifices in every century for the living and dead
opt2: It is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment: so Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation
opt3: It is appointed unto men to vanish into oblivion at physical death: so Christ remains in celestial seclusion without returning to earth
opt4: It is appointed unto men to enter purgatory for cleansing: so Christ returns to condemn all who failed to observe Levitical sabbaths
correct: It is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment: so Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation
explanation: Human destiny is framed by physical death and judgment; corresponding to this, Christ died once for our sins and will return to consummate the salvation of those who await Him. Hebrews 9:27-28 (KJV) - "And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation."

question: According to Hebrews 10:1, why could the law's repetitive annual sacrifices never make the worshipers perfect?
opt1: Because the priests failed to slaughter animals with correct ceremonial bronze knives
opt2: Because Roman soldiers frequently interrupted the sacrifices in the temple court
opt3: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect
opt4: Because the worshipers refused to donate sufficient silver alongside the sacrificial lambs
correct: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect
explanation: The law provided only a foreshadowing rather than the substance; its ceaseless repetition proved that it could never permanently cleanse worshipers. Hebrews 10:1 (KJV) - "For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect."

question: What categorical, definitive theological reality is stated in Hebrews 10:4 concerning animal sacrifices?
opt1: For animal blood permanently erases all guilt before God's judgment seat
opt2: For animal blood purifies the soul whenever accompanied by forty days of fasting
opt3: For animal blood justifies every descendant of Abraham who observes the sabbath
opt4: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins
correct: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins
explanation: The blood of irrational animal substitutes has zero ontological capacity to expiate human moral guilt and remove sins. Hebrews 10:4 (KJV) - "For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins."

question: In Hebrews 10:9-10, what does Christ abolish and establish, and by what means are believers sanctified?
opt1: He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all
opt2: He taketh away the New Covenant, that he may restore the Levitical priesthood. By which we are sanctified through annual animal sacrifices
opt3: He taketh away civil law, that he may establish monastic seclusion. By which we are sanctified through severe physical fasts
opt4: He taketh away moral responsibility, that he may establish philosophical debate. By which we are sanctified through human intellect
correct: He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all
explanation: Christ abolished the Old Covenant animal sacrifice system to establish the New Covenant will of God, sanctifying us once for all through His bodily offering. Hebrews 10:9-10 (KJV) - "Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all."

question: What dramatic contrast in posture and efficacy is highlighted between Levitical priests and Jesus Christ in Hebrews 10:11-12?
opt1: Levitical priests sat down on golden thrones in the temple courts: while Jesus stood continually offering daily sacrifices in heaven
opt2: Every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: but this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God
opt3: Levitical priests offered one sacrifice that ended all sin: while Jesus offers repeated sacrifices throughout the centuries
opt4: Levitical priests entered the holy place without blood: while Jesus offered the blood of bulls on the heavenly altar
correct: Every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: but this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God
explanation: Levitical priests never sat because their work was never done; Christ sat down at God's right hand because His single sacrifice achieved eternal completion. Hebrews 10:11-12 (KJV) - "And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;"

question: In Hebrews 10:14, what did Christ accomplish by His single offering for all who are sanctified?
opt1: He secured temporary pardon until the next annual Day of Atonement
opt2: He provided moral guidance requiring ongoing Levitical sacrifices for perfection
opt3: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified
opt4: He established a preliminary salvation that depends upon human ascetic works
correct: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified
explanation: Christ's single, unrepeatable sacrifice accomplished permanent, finished perfection for all who are set apart in Him. Hebrews 10:14 (KJV) - "For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified."

question: According to Hebrews 10:19-20, what boldness do believers possess, and through what new and living way do we enter?
opt1: Boldness to petition the Roman emperor for civic rights, by a legal appeal through the provincial courts
opt2: Boldness to offer incense in the earthly temple, by permission of the high priest through the court of the priests
opt3: Boldness to ascend Mount Sinai, by climbing through the darkness of the tempest
opt4: Boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh
correct: Boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh
explanation: Through the torn veil of Christ's flesh and His shed blood, believers enjoy joyful, confident access directly into the heavenly Holy of Holies. Hebrews 10:19-20 (KJV) - "Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;"

question: In Hebrews 10:24-25, what mutual community disciplines are commanded, especially as we see the Day approaching?
opt1: Consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another
opt2: Compel one another to pay heavy church tithes: avoiding fellowship with poorer members; and debating theological theories in public markets
opt3: Isolate yourselves in solitary mountain caves: forsaking all public corporate worship; and fasting forty days in silence
opt4: Examine one another for violations of Mosaic dietary laws: delivering offenders to Roman magistrates for punishment
correct: Consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another
explanation: Believers must actively spur one another to love and good deeds, faithfully maintaining church assembly and mutual encouragement as the Lord's return nears. Hebrews 10:24-25 (KJV) - "And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching."

question: According to Hebrews 10:26, what dire spiritual condition results from sinning willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth?
opt1: There remains only minor ecclesiastical penance before full restoration
opt2: There remaineth no more sacrifice for sins
opt3: There remains an obligation to sacrifice two bullocks at the Jerusalem temple
opt4: There remains automatic pardon through ancestral descent from Abraham
correct: There remaineth no more sacrifice for sins
explanation: Deliberate, apostate rejection of Christ's gospel leaves no alternative sacrifice, because Christ is God's only and final remedy for sin. Hebrews 10:26 (KJV) - "For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,"

question: In Hebrews 10:29, what threefold outrage characterizes the apostate who despises the gospel of Christ?
opt1: Refused to learn Greek grammar, violated the municipal health codes of Rome, and failed to attend civic festivals
opt2: Forgotten the genealogies of the patriarchs, broken the fast of the new moon, and neglected to give alms
opt3: Trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace
opt4: Criticized the architectural design of the temple, refused to buy sacrificial doves, and questioned the Sanhedrin
correct: Trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace
explanation: Apostasy represents an unspeakable crime: trampling the Son of God, treating His precious covenant blood as profane, and insulting the gracious Holy Spirit. Hebrews 10:29 (KJV) - "Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?"

question: What solemn, sobering truth regarding divine judgment is proclaimed in Hebrews 10:31?
opt1: It is a pleasant thing to appear before the judgment seat without reconciliation
opt2: It is an impossible thing for the living God to punish unrepentant sinners
opt3: It is a light thing to face divine wrath since all humans are automatically pardoned
opt4: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God
correct: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God
explanation: Falling under the unmitigated judicial wrath of the living God is the most terrifying prospect imaginable for an unrepentant soul. Hebrews 10:31 (KJV) - "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God."

question: What classic, biblical definition of faith opens the great 'Hall of Faith' in Hebrews 11:1?
opt1: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen
opt2: Now faith is the intellectual mastery of philosophical doctrines recorded by ancient sages
opt3: Now faith is the mystical trance attained through prolonged ascetic fasting in the wilderness
opt4: Now faith is the adherence to written civic laws enacted by Roman emperors
correct: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen
explanation: Faith provides present substantial reality to unseen future hopes and tangible conviction regarding spiritual realities invisible to mortal sight. Hebrews 11:1 (KJV) - "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen."

question: According to Hebrews 11:3, what cosmic truth concerning creation do we understand through faith?
opt1: We understand that the cosmos evolved by random chance from eternal primordial matter
opt2: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear
opt3: We understand that the universe was constructed by physical angels using visible planetary materials
opt4: We understand that the world is an eternal illusion with neither beginning nor end
correct: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear
explanation: Faith recognizes creation ex nihilo: the universe was summoned into existence by God's sovereign command out of that which was invisible. Hebrews 11:3 (KJV) - "Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear."

question: In Hebrews 11:4, why was Abel's sacrifice more excellent than Cain's, and what does it still do today?
opt1: Abel offered greater agricultural harvest than Cain, obtaining political honor; and by it he established a kingdom
opt2: Abel built a stone altar in Jerusalem, obtaining priestly titles; and by it he silenced the prophets
opt3: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous; and by it he being dead yet speaketh
opt4: Abel paid silver to the temple treasury, obtaining legal exemptions; and by it he condemned all shepherds
correct: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous; and by it he being dead yet speaketh
explanation: Abel's sacrifice was offered in obedient faith with atoning blood, securing divine witness of righteousness, so that his faithful testimony continues to speak through centuries. Hebrews 11:4 (KJV) - "By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh."

question: According to Hebrews 11:6, why is faith indispensable, and what two foundational convictions must everyone have who comes to God?
opt1: Without wealth it is impossible to approach him: for he that cometh must possess gold, and pay tithes
opt2: Without circumcision it is impossible to worship him: for he that cometh must be born of Abraham, and keep the sabbath
opt3: Without worldly philosophy it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh must master logic, and debate scholars
opt4: Without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him
correct: Without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him
explanation: Faith is the absolute prerequisite to pleasing God, requiring unwavering belief in His existence and trust in His gracious reward for earnest seekers. Hebrews 11:6 (KJV) - "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him."

question: In Hebrews 11:7, what actions did Noah take when divinely warned of things not seen as yet, and what did he become?
opt1: Moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith
opt2: Moved with doubt, fled into the mountains of Ararat to hide from mortal neighbors
opt3: Moved with pride, built a stone tower in Babel to make a great name for himself
opt4: Moved with anger, waged physical warfare against the wicked giants of the earth
correct: Moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith
explanation: Reverent faith prompted Noah to obey God's warning regarding unseen judgment, building the ark, rebuking an unbelieving world, and inheriting righteousness. Hebrews 11:7 (KJV) - "By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith."

question: According to Hebrews 11:8-10, what eternal celestial dwelling was Abraham looking for as he sojourned in tents in the land of promise?
opt1: He looked for an earthly stone fortress constructed by the architects of Egypt
opt2: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God
opt3: He looked for a grand marble palace built by the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah
opt4: He looked for a municipal capital granted to his descendants by Roman imperial decree
correct: For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God
explanation: Abraham lived as a pilgrim in temporary tents because his ultimate hope was anchored in the New Jerusalem, designed and built by God Himself. Hebrews 11:10 (KJV) - "For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God."

question: In Hebrews 11:17-19, what supreme theological calculation enabled Abraham to offer up Isaac on the altar?
opt1: Accounting that he could easily father other sons to replace Isaac if he died
opt2: Accounting that the angel of the Lord would refuse to let the knife strike
opt3: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure
opt4: Accounting that an animal would miraculously appear on the mount before the sacrifice
correct: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure
explanation: Abraham's faith in God's covenant promise was so absolute that he believed God would raise Isaac bodily from ashes, receiving him back figuratively from death. Hebrews 11:17-19 (KJV) - "By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son, Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called: Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure."

question: What radical choice of faith did Moses make when he came of age, as recorded in Hebrews 11:24-26?
opt1: Accepted the royal crown of Egypt; using imperial armies to emancipate the Hebrew slaves by physical force
opt2: Demanded gold and silver from Pharaoh's treasury; living in luxury while sending charity to his brethren
opt3: Fled Egypt to study philosophy in Greece; seeking academic credentials to negotiate with Pharaoh
opt4: Refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt
correct: Refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt
explanation: Moses renounced royal palace prestige and fleeting sinful pleasures, embracing the reproach of Christ as infinitely superior to all Egypt's treasures. Hebrews 11:24-26 (KJV) - "By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward."

question: In Hebrews 11:31, why did the harlot Rahab perish not with them that believed not when Jericho was destroyed?
opt1: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace
opt2: Because she paid large quantities of silver to Joshua's captains before the battle
opt3: Because she was born of the priestly tribe of Levi and knew the law of Moses
opt4: Because she fought alongside the armies of Israel using Canaanite weapons
correct: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace
explanation: Rahab's saving faith in the God of Israel was demonstrated by sheltering the Hebrew spies, delivering her household from Jericho's annihilation. Hebrews 11:31 (KJV) - "By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace."

question: According to Hebrews 11:39-40, why did all these Old Testament heroes of faith not receive the full promise in their lifetime?
opt1: Because their faith was defective and failed to please God in their generation
opt2: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect
opt3: Because the Roman Empire had not yet established universal roads across the provinces
opt4: Because they refused to offer sufficient animal sacrifices on the Day of Atonement
correct: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect
explanation: God orchestrated redemptive history so that Old Testament saints would achieve consummate perfection only alongside New Testament believers in Christ. Hebrews 11:39-40 (KJV) - "And these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise: God having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect."

question: Surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses in Hebrews 12:1, what two things are believers commanded to lay aside as they run the race set before them?
opt1: Let us lay aside all physical food, and all earthly clothing, and let us run in solitary deserts
opt2: Let us lay aside the holy scriptures, and all apostolic epistles, and let us run after Greek philosophy
opt3: Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us
opt4: Let us lay aside our manual trades, and all civic responsibilities, and let us run into monasteries
correct: Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us
explanation: Christian life is an endurance race requiring us to strip away every distracting encumbrance and entangling sin, running with patient fortitude. Hebrews 12:1 (KJV) - "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,"

question: According to Hebrews 12:2, upon whom must our gaze be fixed, and what sustained Him through the shame and agony of the cross?
opt1: Looking unto Moses the lawgiver; who for fear of divine wrath carved stone tablets on the mount
opt2: Looking unto Joshua the general; who for the thrill of military triumph subdued the Canaanites
opt3: Looking unto Aaron the high priest; who for the beauty of golden robes offered incense in the tent
opt4: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God
correct: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God
explanation: Jesus is the pioneer and perfecter of faith, whose endurance through the shame of the cross was fueled by the anticipated joy of redeeming His people. Hebrews 12:2 (KJV) - "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."

question: In Hebrews 12:4, what perspective does the author provide to challenge the Hebrew believers regarding their struggle against sin?
opt1: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin
opt2: Ye have already sacrificed all your mortal lives upon Roman altars
opt3: Ye have already conquered all physical temptations and reached sinless perfection
opt4: Ye have already defeated all persecutors using physical weapons in battle
correct: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin
explanation: Though enduring hardship, the readers had not yet suffered martyrdom (resisted unto blood), urging them to maintain persevering courage. Hebrews 12:4 (KJV) - "Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin."

question: According to Hebrews 12:6, what does divine chastening fundamentally prove regarding the believer's standing before God?
opt1: That God has rejected the believer and transferred his inheritance to another
opt2: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth
opt3: That the believer has committed the unpardonable sin and is doomed to wrath
opt4: That God treats believers as hostile enemies deserving eternal damnation
correct: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth
explanation: Lordly discipline is not punitive hatred, but the unmistakable evidence of the Father's profound love and genuine family adoption. Hebrews 12:6 (KJV) - "For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth."

question: In Hebrews 12:11, how does chastening feel in the present, and what glorious fruit does it produce afterward in those trained by it?
opt1: It feels comfortable and effortless; yielding worldly wealth and earthly fame
opt2: It feels painless and joyful; yielding automatic exemption from future trials
opt3: No chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby
opt4: It feels destructive and fatal; yielding bitter despair and spiritual ruin
correct: No chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby
explanation: Though discipline is temporarily painful, it trains and refines the soul to bear a rich harvest of peaceable righteousness. Hebrews 12:11 (KJV) - "Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby."

question: According to Hebrews 12:14, what two spiritual pursuits are commanded, without which no man shall see the Lord?
opt1: Follow worldly wealth, and political influence, without which no man shall enter Rome
opt2: Follow ceremonial washings, and dietary laws, without which no man shall enter the temple
opt3: Follow public debate, and Greek rhetoric, without which no man shall convince scholars
opt4: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord
correct: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord
explanation: Believers are called to pursue harmonious relationships with all people and uncompromising personal holiness as the indispensable condition for seeing God. Hebrews 12:14 (KJV) - "Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:"

question: In Hebrews 12:16-17, what tragic warning is drawn from the profane choice of Esau?
opt1: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected
opt2: Esau sold his flock to Egyptian merchants, and was denied entrance into the land of Canaan
opt3: Esau built an altar to pagan idols in Edom, and was struck with leprosy by the prophet
opt4: Esau refused to marry daughters of the Canaanites, and was disinherited by Isaac
correct: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected
explanation: Esau despised sacred, eternal spiritual privileges for a single temporary physical meal, finding no way to reverse the irrevocable loss though he sought it with tears. Hebrews 12:16-17 (KJV) - "Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears."

question: According to Hebrews 12:18-21, what terrifying physical phenomena characterized Mount Sinai under the Old Covenant?
opt1: A quiet green meadow surrounded by peaceful streams where angels sang joyful anthems
opt2: The mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest
opt3: A marble city adorned with golden arches where kings gathered for festive banquets
opt4: A calm blue lake where fishermen cast nets without fear of thunder or storms
correct: The mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest
explanation: Mount Sinai represented the terrors of the law: tangible, blazing with consuming fire, cloaked in darkness, gale-force winds, and shattering trumpet blasts. Hebrews 12:18 (KJV) - "For ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,"

question: In triumphant contrast to Mount Sinai, to what glorious celestial reality have New Covenant believers come in Hebrews 12:22-24?
opt1: Unto the earthly city of Athens, to the stoic philosophers in the academy, to Roman magistrates
opt2: Unto the wilderness tabernacle in the desert of Zin, to the tent of Moses and the sons of Aaron
opt3: Unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn... and to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel
opt4: Unto the municipal amphitheaters of Ephesus, to public games and gladiatorial contests
correct: Unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn... and to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel
explanation: Believers do not approach a mountain of terror, but Mount Zion: the joyful, triumphant assembly of heaven, the living God, Jesus the Mediator, and His cleansing blood that speaks grace rather than vengeance. Hebrews 12:22-24 (KJV) - "But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel."

question: According to Hebrews 12:28-29, receiving an unshakable kingdom, how must we serve God, and what solemn truth describes His nature?
opt1: Let us demand earthly tribute from civil magistrates: for our God is an earthly monarch
opt2: Let us live in carefree indifference without moral boundaries: for our God overlooks all sin
opt3: Let us build stone monuments in every province: for our God delights in physical architecture
opt4: Let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: for our God is a consuming fire
correct: Let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: for our God is a consuming fire
explanation: Citizens of God's unshakable kingdom are called to reverent, awe-filled worship, remembering that our holy God is an all-consuming fire. Hebrews 12:28-29 (KJV) - "Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: For our God is a consuming fire."

question: In Hebrews 13:1-2, what community virtues are commanded, and what remarkable privilege occurred through entertaining strangers?
opt1: Let brotherly love continue. Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares
opt2: Let political ambition increase. Be not slow to litigate against strangers: for thereby some have won lawsuits
opt3: Let commercial trade expand. Be not hesitant to sell goods to strangers: for thereby some gained riches
opt4: Let monastic silence reign. Be not willing to speak to strangers: for thereby some avoided persecution
correct: Let brotherly love continue. Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares
explanation: Christian brotherhood must flourish through generous hospitality to traveling strangers, recalling Abraham and Lot who unknowingly hosted angels. Hebrews 13:1-2 (KJV) - "Let brotherly love continue. Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares."

question: According to Hebrews 13:4, how is marriage regarded by God, and who will face divine judgment?
opt1: Marriage is a carnal compromise for weak believers: but celibate ascetics alone will inherit heaven
opt2: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge
opt3: Marriage is a temporary municipal contract: but civil courts alone will judge marital infidelity
opt4: Marriage is forbidden to all who serve as elders: but single ministers God will elevate above angels
correct: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge
explanation: Scripture upholds marriage as honorable and pure, while issuing an unequivocal warning that sexual immorality and adultery will face divine judgment. Hebrews 13:4 (KJV) - "Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge."

question: In Hebrews 13:5, what attitude toward material wealth is commanded, and what precious divine promise grounds our contentment?
opt1: Let your lifestyle seek abundant gold; and be dissatisfied until you own estates: for God promises worldly wealth
opt2: Let your conversation be filled with commercial trade; and borrow silver from lenders: for money shields from trials
opt3: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee
opt4: Let your ambitions dominate your thoughts; and hoard food in barns: for physical provision guarantees peace
correct: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee
explanation: Freedom from covetousness and genuine contentment spring from God's personal, unbreakable pledge: 'I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.' Hebrews 13:5 (KJV) - "Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee."

question: According to Hebrews 13:7, how should church members honor spiritual leaders who have passed on after preaching God's Word?
opt1: Erect marble statues in their memory in public theaters, and worship their relics with incense
opt2: Examine their financial ledgers, and divide their personal estates among the city elders
opt3: Re-write their doctrines, and adapt their sermons to conform to fashionable Greek philosophy
opt4: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation
correct: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation
explanation: Believers are called to remember departed pastoral leaders, imitate their steadfast faith, and ponder the holy culmination of their life's conduct. Hebrews 13:7 (KJV) - "Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation."

question: What timeless, immutable Christological declaration is proclaimed in Hebrews 13:8?
opt1: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever
opt2: Jesus Christ changes His doctrine according to the shifting cultures of human empires
opt3: Jesus Christ was a prophet yesterday, an angel today, and an earthly king tomorrow
opt4: Jesus Christ evolves His character through observing the historical struggles of the church
correct: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever
explanation: In a fluctuating, uncertain world, Jesus Christ remains eternally constant, unchanging in His divine nature, His redemptive power, and His covenant love. Hebrews 13:8 (KJV) - "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever."

question: In Hebrews 13:9, with what is it good for the human heart to be established, rather than divers and strange doctrines?
opt1: It is a good thing that the heart be established with Levitical dietary laws and new moon fasts
opt2: It is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein
opt3: It is a good thing that the heart be established with Greek logic and philosophical stoicism
opt4: It is a good thing that the heart be established with Roman citizenship and imperial tax privileges
correct: It is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein
explanation: Spiritual stability is forged by God's inward transforming grace, not by external dietary taboos or ritualistic food regulations that yield zero spiritual profit. Hebrews 13:9 (KJV) - "Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein."

question: According to Hebrews 13:12-13, where did Jesus suffer to sanctify the people with His own blood, and what call is extended to us?
opt1: Jesus suffered in the innermost sanctuary of the temple; let us therefore observe all Levitical ceremonies within Jerusalem
opt2: Jesus suffered in the palace of Pontius Pilate; let us therefore seek political influence within the Roman Senate
opt3: Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach
opt4: Jesus suffered upon the pinnacle of Mount Sinai; let us therefore build stone altars within the wilderness
correct: Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach
explanation: Just as sin offerings were burned outside the camp, Jesus was crucified outside Jerusalem's gates, summoning believers to step outside worldly religious systems to share His reproach. Hebrews 13:12-13 (KJV) - "Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach."

question: In Hebrews 13:15, what spiritual sacrifice are New Covenant believers commanded to offer to God continually by Christ?
opt1: Let us offer the blood of calves and lambs at annual religious festivals in Jerusalem
opt2: Let us offer burning incense twice daily upon golden altars inside stone sanctuaries
opt3: Let us offer forty days of solitary fasting in wilderness caves without water
opt4: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name
correct: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name
explanation: The Christian's sacrificial offering is not slaughtered animals, but perpetual praise and joyful thanksgiving pouring from lips consecrated to His name. Hebrews 13:15 (KJV) - "By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name."

question: According to Hebrews 13:17, why are believers instructed to obey and submit to their spiritual leaders?
opt1: For they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you
opt2: Because spiritual leaders possess civil authority to seize the property of rebellious members
opt3: Because spiritual leaders are immune to error and have memorized the entire oral law
opt4: Because spiritual leaders collect civic taxes on behalf of the Roman provincial government
correct: For they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you
explanation: Pastoral leaders carry the sobering weight of watching over souls to give an account to God; believers should cooperate so their oversight is a joy rather than a burden. Hebrews 13:17 (KJV) - "Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you."

question: What majestic closing benediction crowns the epistle in Hebrews 13:20-21?
opt1: Now the Roman emperor, supreme ruler of nations, grant you diplomatic immunity and peace throughout your provinces
opt2: Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ
opt3: Now the angels of heaven, who spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, keep you under the ceremonial yoke of the law
opt4: Now the high priest of Jerusalem, who offers blood on the earthly altar, forgive your sins through animal sacrifices
correct: Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ
explanation: The author commits the church to the God of peace who resurrected our Great Shepherd Jesus through the everlasting covenant blood, praying for total spiritual equipping to do His will. Hebrews 13:20-21 (KJV) - "Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen."
